newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka insurance to cover Jaffna.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka insurance to cover Jaffna.

text.p: State-owned Sri Lanka Insurance Corp (SLIC) said on Tuesday it had reintroduced limited insurance schemes in the former Tamil Tiger rebel stronghold of Jaffna after a seven-year break.

Chairman Jagath Wickremasinghe told Reuters the cessation of hostilities in the northern peninsula after its recapture by government forces in 1996 had allowed the company to offer non-life cover up to 10 million rupees ($170,600).

"Once the army recaptured Jaffna, Her Excellency the President (Chandrika Kumaratunga) asked me to consider extending cover to this area. So we have now extended a limited service," Wickremasinghe said in an interview.

The Sri Lankan government is fighting a 13-year-old war against Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who demand a separate homeland for the minority Tamil population in the island's north and east.
Government forces captured Jaffna town in December 1995 and wrested control of the entire peninsula four months later, pushing the rebels further into the Wanni region.
The government said two weeks ago nearly 500,000 civilians who fled the war have returned to Jaffna and reconstruction work in the once devastated area was in full swing.
Parliament voted last week to end a state of emergency across much of the country after a drop in violent incidents.
The state of emergency remains in the capital, Colombo, and surrounding areas and in northern and eastern provinces.
Wickremasinghe said his company was offering insurance cover for property, vehicles and other general policies in Jaffna.
"For the last seven years we gave no general -- non-life -- insurance in Jaffna. But I gave instructions two weeks ago to the regional manager to resume. So far we have had no big claims," he said.
He said the ceiling of 10 million rupees was determined by the amount SLIC could cover through domestic reinsurance.
"Above 10 million rupees would require foreign reinsurance," he said. He declined to say if the ceiling would eventually be raised or removed.

He said SLIC had continued to operate in Jaffna throughout the ethnic conflict, offering life-assurance policies, except for a brief period in early 1996 when the battle for the peninsula was at its height.
SLIC is one of two state-owned insurance firms and one of only five companies licensed to operate in Sri Lanka.
The government has said it will liberalise the insurance industry and divest minority and majority stakes in areas of financial services.
But Wickremasinghe said he was not aware of any plans to sell the government's 100 percent holding in his firm. ($1 = 58.6 rupees)
